text:
elaine-support: Hey team — Acme reports that after migrating to OIDC their scheduled job can no longer fetch audit logs. Calls to /v1/audit/logs now return a 401 with "insufficient_scope: audit.logs.read". Other API endpoints still work for them.

bob-acme: (customer) We moved to OIDC this morning and our cron started failing. Example response below.

bob-acme: ```
GET https://api.redwood.ai/v1/audit/logs?org=acme-corp
Authorization: Bearer <oauth_access_token>

HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json

{"error":"insufficient_scope","message":"token missing scope: audit.logs.read"}
```

tom-infra: Two things to check: (1) does the access token include the audit scope after exchange, and (2) does the org have the audit entitlement and retention bucket enabled. Can you paste the decoded token claims (redact PII)?

bob-acme: Decoded token shows claim "scp": ["openid","profile","email","api.read"] — no audit scope.

anita-idp: On the IdP side, the client registration may be filtering scopes or the consent policy is stripping non-standard scopes. Also some IdPs map group membership into scopes — confirm client allowed scopes include "audit.logs.read".

elaine-support: On our side, the OAuth exchange only returns requested scopes that the client is permitted to have and the user consented to. Additionally, our API enforces both token scope and org entitlement for audit access. Missing either will block access.

lee-security: Note: missing token scope returns 401 with insufficient_scope. When org entitlement missing we sometimes return 403 or empty results depending on retention config. We should surface clearer messaging to customers.

tom-infra: Repro steps for internal debugging:
``
# simulate token exchange requesting audit scope
curl -X POST https://oauth.redwood.ai/token \
 -d "grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:jwt-bearer" \
 -d "scope=openid profile email api.read audit.logs.read" \
 -d "client_id=acme-client" \
 -d "assertion=<saml-assertion>"
```
Then inspect the "scp" claim in the returned access_token.

elaine-support: Customer-facing remediation options:
1) Update OIDC client registration / IdP policy so tokens include "audit.logs.read" (ask IdP to allow that scope).
2) As a hotfix, we can issue a short-lived service token scoped to "audit.logs.read" for their cron job.

bob-acme: We want a hotfix while our IdP team updates client registration. Can you issue a temporary token?

tom-infra: Internal service token creation (admin only):
``
POST /admin/v1/service_tokens
Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN
{
  "org_id":"acme-corp",
  "name":"acme-cron-audit-temp",
  "scopes":["audit.logs.read"],
  "expires_in":3600
}
```
We will return the token and schedule rotation.

anita-idp: Also verify if the client has "consent_required" true; some IdPs drop non-standard scopes if consent is not set.

lee-security: I checked entitlements for acme-corp (internal):
``
GET https://console.redwood.ai/admin/v1/orgs/acme-corp/entitlements
# response: {"org_id":"acme-corp","entitlements":["api.read","logging.basic"]}
```
So "audit.read" is missing. I'll file ENT-310 to add the entitlement and enable an audit retention bucket (temp 7 days) once approved.

oncall-bot: @lee-security scheduled ENT-310 for 2026-04-02T09:30:00Z

elaine-support: Shared both options with the customer. They accepted the temp service token; cron started succeeding immediately. We've asked them to update OIDC client registration and confirm so we can revoke the token.

bob-acme: Confirmed the service token works and shows logs flowing. We'll update our IdP and notify you to revoke the temp token.

lee-security: Post-incident actions: update docs to call out the distinction between token scopes and org entitlements for audit access; improve error messages to differentiate missing token scope vs missing org entitlement; add an alert when orgs have active audit integrations but lack "audit.read" entitlement.

elaine-support: Closing once customer confirms IdP change and we revoke the temp token. Thanks all :rocket:
